title: Affine-Profile Stabilizer Thresholds for Magic in Codeword-Stabilized Quantum Codes
abstract: Codeword-stabilized quantum codes give a unified graph-state description of stabilizer and nonadditive quantum error-correcting codes. Although each individual CWS word state is stabilizer, coherent superpositions of different word states can be nonstabilizer. We develop a CWS-adapted magic-witness framework that isolates this codeword coherence and converts it into certified lower bounds on robustness of magic.   The main result is an exact reduction of the stabilizer threshold of a natural CWS coherence witness to a finite-geometric problem over the classical CWS word set. For general weighted superpositions, the threshold is computed by enumerating affine intersections and affine-quadratic phases. For equal-weight superpositions, the phase optimization collapses, and the threshold is determined entirely by how many CWS words can lie in affine flats of each dimension. Thus a quantum optimization over stabilizer states becomes a classical affine-incidence problem.   This reduction yields a fixed-parameter algorithm, an analytic lower bound for an infinite union-stabilizer family, and exact rational certificates for several standard nonadditive CWS examples. The framework also clarifies why exact enumeration fails for large structured families and identifies the remaining task as an affine-intersection problem. The result provides a geometric mechanism by which nonlinear CWS word sets generate certifiable magic.
summary: This paper introduces a novel geometric framework to determine the robustness of magic for quantum states encoded by Codeword-Stabilized codes. By developing a CWS-adapted magic-witness, the authors reduce a complex quantum optimization problem to a tractable classical affine-incidence problem. This yields precise, computable lower bounds on quantum resource robustness based purely on the geometry of the underlying classical word set.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to compute lower bounds on the robustness of magic ($R(ho)$) for quantum states arising from Codeword-Stabilized (CWS) codes.
main_result: The quantum optimization problem is exactly reduced to a classical affine-incidence problem over the CWS word set, providing a fixed-parameter algorithm for calculating the stabilizer threshold.
method: The authors use a CWS-adapted magic-witness framework to isolate codeword coherence, converting the quantum optimization into a geometric problem involving affine intersections of the classical word set.
model_or_system: The model involves CWS codes, which provide a unified graph-state description for both stabilizer and non-additive quantum error-correcting codes. The states analyzed are coherent superpositions of individual word states.
key_observables: Robustness of magic ($R(ho)$), the stabilizer threshold ($ eta_{	ext{coh}}$), and the affine-intersection profile $M_r(C)$.
important_parameters: The size of the word set ($K$), the number of qubits ($n$), and the structure of the classical word set $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$.
main_assumptions: The certificate relies on calibrated Pauli measurements and is a magic witness, not a device-independent Bell inequality. The analysis is most meaningful when the target state is the coherent CWS superposition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lower-bound principle using CHSH/W-type scans, comparing exact RoM versus the calculated lower bound.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the coherence witness, deriving the general bound, specializing to the equal-weight case where phase optimization collapses, and finally establishing the exact reduction to the classical affine-incidence problem.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful geometric tool (affine geometry) to analyze quantum resource bounds (magic robustness) in QEC codes, connecting abstract quantum optimization to concrete classical combinatorial problems.
